properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 3 at 5:42PM MST until August 3 at 6:45PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
SVRTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southwestern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...
East Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...
Eastern Santa Cruz County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 645 PM MST.

* At 542 PM MST, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
7 miles east of Parker Canyon Lake to near Kartchner Caverns State
Park, moving west at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Sierra Vista, Hereford, Whetstone, Huachuca City, Patagonia,
Sonoita, Elgin, Fort Huachuca, Parker Canyon Lake, Kartchner
Caverns State Park, Canelo, Ramsey Canyon Preserve, Lochiel and
Coronado National Memorial.

This includes the following highways...
Route 90 between mile markers 296 and 319. Route 92 between mile
markers 322 and 335. Route 82 between mile markers 20 and 57. Route
83 between mile markers 3 and 42...and between mile markers 50 and
52.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Lightning is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can
hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.
properties.area: Cochise, AZ; Pima, AZ; Santa Cruz, AZ

properties.description:

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lynchburg...                       Bedford...
Glasgow...                         Big Island...
Forest...                          Montvale...
Sedalia...

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Bold Branch, Back Creek, Big Otter River and Back Run.
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather

Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.title: Dust Storm Warning issued August 3 at 4:28PM MST until August 3 at 6:30PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Dust Storm Warning for...
Northeastern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 630 PM MST.

* At 428 PM MST, an area of blowing dust was located near San Simon,
moving west southwest 10 to 15 mph.

HAZARD...Less than a quarter mile visibility with strong winds in
excess of 60 mph.

SOURCE...Detected by National Weather Service meteorologists and
cameras in the area.

IMPACT...Dangerous life-threatening travel.

* Locations impacted include...
Willcox, Portal, Bowie, Dragoon, Chiricahua National Monument,
Pearce-Sunsites, Cochise, Sunizona, Kansas Settlement, San Simon,
Paradise and Texas Canyon.

This includes the following highways...
Route 181 between mile markers 39 and 64. Route 191 between mile
markers 36 and 92. Interstate 10 between mile markers 316 and 390.
Route 186 between mile markers 327 and 359.
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not drive into a dust storm. PULL ASIDE STAY ALIVE!

Dust storms lead to dangerous driving conditions with visibility
reduced to near zero. If driving, avoid dust storms if possible. If
caught in one, pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep your
foot off the brake.

To report hazardous dust conditions, contact the National Weather
Service, or your nearest law enforcement agency, who will relay your
report to the National Weather Service office in Tucson AZ.

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued August 3 at 11:03AM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from good to moderate, but is forecasted to degrade.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM Wednesday, August 5, 2026.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare

health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 3 at 9:17AM CDT until August 6 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 37.3 feet, Widespread lowland flooding occurs. Minor
roads are closed. Airport Road boat ramp near Live Oak County
Airport is flooded and closed. Major flooding occurs in the River
Creek Acres Subdivision, with several feet of water and several
homes flooded. Residents in the J.I. Hailey Subdivision at Jones
River bend have trouble getting out as water covers much of
Antelope Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Monday the stage was 37.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall into moderate flood
stage Tuesday, then fall below flood stage midday Thursday. The
river will then continue to fall to 12.8 feet Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
